AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Data on the cost and efficiency of skin cancer detection through total body skin examination (TBSE) are scarce.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To determine the number needed to screen (NNS) and biopsy (NNB) and cost per skin cancer diagnosed in a large dermatology practice in patients undergoing TBSE.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: From 2011 - 2015, 20,270 patients underwent 33,647 visits for TBSE; 9956 lesion biopsies were performed yielding 2,763 skin cancers, including 155 melanomas. The NNS to detect one skin cancer was 12.2 (95% CI 11.7-12.6) and one melanoma was 215 (95% CI 185-252). The NNB to detect one skin cancer was 3.0 (95% CI 2.9-3.1) and one melanoma was 27.8 (95% CI 23.3-33.3). In a multivariable model for NNS, age and personal history of melanoma were significant factors. Age switches from a protective to a risk factor at 51 years. The estimated cost per melanoma detected was $32,594 (95% CI $27,326-$37,475).

AbstractText.Label: LIMITATIONS
AbstractText.content: Data are from a single healthcare system and based on physician coding.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Melanoma detection through TBSE is most efficient in patients over age 50 and those with a personal history of melanoma. Our findings will be helpful in modeling the cost effectiveness of melanoma screening by dermatologists.
